title: Structs: NULL fields equal in `=` and grouping; in order a NULL field is the greatest, also in `<`
verdict: structural equality, NULL = NULL inside; `<` two-valued with NULL greatest
description: `{'a': 1, 'b': NULL} = {'a': 1, 'b': NULL}` is true, and so is `[1, NULL] = [1, NULL]`: a NULL inside a struct or list equals NULL. A NULL struct or list compared with anything is NULL. Grouping and joins on struct keys put equal structs, NULL fields included, together.

Order is field by field, a NULL field after every value, in comparisons as in `ORDER BY`: `{a: 1, b: NULL} < {a: 1, b: 2}` is false and `>` true; ascending order puts `{a: NULL, b: 0}` last and descending first.
The docs are silent on a NULL struct compared with anything giving NULL: a docs gap.
reference: Equality is structural, and NULLs inside lists and structs are equal, as in grouping (reference-semantics.md, NULL and Nested). Lists order element by element, three-valued in `<` (a NULL element that decides gives NULL) and NULL greatest in `ORDER BY` (#207); DuckDB's lists are two-valued in `<` (R11, shimmed with `list_lt`). Structs are the lists of their fields, so the same split would hold.
DuckDB's SQL refuses struct columns and fields for now (docs/nested-values.md), so no written plan compares structs.

a NULL struct compared with any operator → NULL
NULL entries in the same position are equal; a NULL entry is larger than any non-NULL value
